Party Frame Analysis in the House of Commons¶

This notebook explores how political parties frame Brexit-related debates in the UK House of Commons using the annotated chunks stored in thesis_final.duckdb. We focus on MPs whose party affiliation can be retrieved from MPS, highlighting the four major parties (Conservative, Labour, Liberal Democrat, Scottish National Party) and aggregating all remaining MPs under “Other”. The goal is to identify distinctive framing profiles per party and to understand how framing aligns with Leave/Remain positions.

Data Coverage¶

Observation: the annotated dataset predominantly covers Conservative and Labour MPs. Liberal Democrats appear only marginally and there are currently no annotated chunks for the Scottish National Party. All subsequent analyses therefore focus on the four target parties, while noting that results for parties with few samples (especially Liberal Democrats and SNP) remain tentative.

Takeaways: Conservatives dominate the available annotations and lean towards conflict and economic frames, while Labour highlights human impact and moral value frames. Liberal Democrat coverage remains sparse and the Scottish National Party currently lacks annotated chunks, so results for those parties should be interpreted as placeholders until more data is labelled.

Remain-aligned MPs (mostly Labour) still emphasise human impact and moral concerns, whereas Leave supporters highlight economic and conflict frames. Further annotations are needed for a balanced comparison.

Distinctive Frame Analysis¶

Which frames differ significantly when we contrast each party against all remaining parties? For every party we run a chi-square test of independence across frames, report p-values and Cramér's V as the effect size, and then inspect the standardized residuals per frame to identify over- and under-representations.

Interpretation: Der Chi-Quadrat-Test und Cramers V zeigen, wo sich die Frame-Verteilungen einer Partei deutlich von der Gesamtheit unterscheiden. Positive standardisierte Residuen heben Überrepräsentationen hervor (negative Werte Unterrepräsentationen). Conservatives weisen weiterhin starke Konflikt- und Wirtschaftsanteile auf, Labour betont Human-Impact- und Moral-Frames. Ergebnisse für Liberal Democrats bleiben wegen der kleinen Stichprobe unsicher, und für die Scottish National Party fehlen nach wie vor annotierte Beiträge.

Wrap-up & Next Steps¶

  • The current annotations almost exclusively cover Conservative and Labour MPs; Liberal Democrats appear sporadically and the Scottish National Party is missing altogether. Additional labelling from MPS members is essential for balanced party comparisons.
  • Within the available sample, Conservatives emphasise conflict and economic frames, while Labour leans towards human impact and moral value frames.
  • Leave-supporting MPs (predominantly Conservatives) focus on economic and conflict frames, whereas Remain MPs (mostly Labour) highlight human impact. However, the Leave/Remain sample remains uneven and should be expanded.
  • Future work: backfill missing parties, incorporate constituency-level metadata from MPS, and analyse intra-party splits (Leave vs. Remain MPs within a party) once more annotated chunks become available.
